name: Toxic-Comment-Multi-Label-Classifier
description: Multi-label toxicity detection across 6 categories using TF-IDF + Logistic Regression — trained on 159K real Wikipedia comments (mean ROC-AUC 0.975), served via FastAPI with an interactive Streamlit demo.

paragraphs: A multi-label toxic comment classification system — a single comment can simultaneously trigger multiple toxicity categories (toxic, severetoxic, obscene, threat, insult, identityhate), which is a fundamentally different ML problem from single-label classification: different loss structure, different evaluation metrics, and a model built per label rather than one shared decision boundary.

⚠️ This project processes real user-generated text that includes profanity, slurs, and abusive language as part of its function — that's the nature of a toxicity classifier trained on real labeled toxic content.
features: TF-IDF (word 1-2 grams, 30,000 features, sublinear term frequency
scaling, English stopwords removed) — the primary signal.
Engineered metadata features — comment length, exclamation/question

mark counts, ALL-CAPS ratio, unique-word ratio, average word length. These are cheap, interpretable, and historically useful in toxicity detection (e.g. shouting in all-caps correlates weakly but genuinely with toxicity…
The two feature families are combined via sparse hstack into a single 30,007-dimension matrix fed to all downstream models.
